title: Rahul Dravid Buys Into Dublin Guardians, Takes Cricket to Europe
excerpt: The former India captain joins Abhishek Bachchan in co-owning an ETPL franchise as the sport expands beyond traditional strongholds
body:
Rahul Dravid, the man who coached India to its 2024 T20 World Cup triumph, has traded the dugout for the boardroom — and a rather unexpected geography. The former India captain is now co-owner of the Dublin Guardians, one of six franchises in the European T20 Premier League (ETPL), the continent's first ICC-sanctioned T20 franchise competition.

**Cricket's European Beachhead**

The ETPL, launching in August 2026, spans six cities — Dublin, Belfast, Edinburgh, Glasgow, Rotterdam, and Amsterdam — with 33 matches across a roughly five-week window. Bollywood actor Abhishek Bachchan is among the league's co-founders, and the player roster already boasts names like Glenn Maxwell, Mitchell Marsh, Chris Gayle, and Steve Waugh. Ravichandran Ashwin will captain Dravid's Dublin side, a pairing that recalls India's cerebral cricket tradition. The franchise is valued at roughly £11.1 million, a fraction of IPL franchise prices but a meaningful bet on Europe's untapped cricket market.

**Why Europe, Why Now?**

Cricket Ireland, Cricket Scotland, and the Royal Dutch Cricket Association are all backing the venture, motivated by a simple reality: T20 franchise leagues have become the sport's economic engine everywhere else. India's IPL generates billions; South Africa's SA20 and the UAE's ILT20 are growing fast. Europe, home to sizable South Asian diasporas in the UK, Ireland, and the Netherlands, has been conspicuously absent from this franchise boom. The ETPL aims to bridge that gap by combining grassroots development with star power.

Dravid himself framed his involvement in developmental terms. *'Cricket has enormous potential in Europe,'* he said in a statement, emphasizing the league's focus on nurturing local talent alongside international marquee players.

**The Diaspora Connection**

For the estimated 1.8 million people of Indian origin living across the UK and Ireland, the ETPL is more than entertainment — it is a cultural anchor. Cricket has long been the social glue of South Asian communities in Britain and increasingly in Ireland, where the Indian-born population has surged in recent years. Dravid's name on a Dublin franchise gives the league instant credibility in exactly the communities it needs to reach. Indian-Americans with family ties across the Atlantic will find another reason to track European cricket, particularly with Ashwin leading the charge.

**What to Watch**

The league's inaugural season runs August through September 2026. Whether ETPL can sustain itself beyond the first edition will depend on broadcast deals, local attendance, and whether Cricket Ireland can convert franchise enthusiasm into grassroots participation.
